validated_work_order.understanding: PR #9 (squash commit 026f8b6) fixed a user-visible custom-report bug — with 'Show empty rows' enabled, the report's row axis was built from the raw unfiltered categories, so unchecked categories rendered as phantom 0.00 rows — and merged with nothing under upcoming-release-notes/. The repository requires a note for every user-facing change (packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:105, and .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md line 19 carries `- [ ] Release notes added`). I verified the gap on main: 92 notes exist, none describing this fix; the only custom-report notes are fix-custom-report-legend-scroll.md (chart height) and fix-weekly-report-final-bucket.md (weekly final-week data), both different defects. The contract is the release-note front matter, and I read its enforcement: packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs validates `category` (after categoryAutocorrections) against categoryOrder, requires a non-empty `authors` array of real people (NON_PERSON_AUTHORS = ['claude','github-actions'], plus any login ending `[bot]`), and requires a body of exactly one non-empty line. Up to 0 authors, wrong category, or a wrapped paragraph each fail it. This is one markdown file; there is no second surface.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The PR that shipped the fix did not add a release note, and nothing in CI fails on a missing one here: the composite action .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml exists but is referenced by no workflow in .github/ (grep for 'release-notes' across every workflow returns only sdlc-release.yml's unrelated release-publishing job, zero hits in ci-verify.yml). The requirement in the docs is therefore advisory, and a squashed bot-authored PR slipped past it.
validated_work_order.approach:
Add one file, `upcoming-release-notes/fix-custom-report-show-empty-rows-categories.md`, written by hand with exactly the bytes below. Do NOT run `yarn generate:release-notes` — bin/release-note-generator.mts is an interactive `prompts` session (it asks four questions on stdin and calls `gh api user`), which a non-interactive implementer cannot answer; the issue permits writing the file by hand.

Exact content:

---
category: Bugfix
authors: [Shivam-Fl]
---

Fix custom reports listing categories that were unchecked: with "Show empty rows" enabled, the report now shows only the categories you selected, and spending the selection hid no longer goes missing from the totals.

Three constraints the gate enforces, each of which silently fails a plausible-looking note:

1. `category: Bugfix` is accepted verbatim — the checker autocorrects it to `Bugfixes` before comparing against categoryOrder, and `Bugfix` is also what packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md lists as valid. Do not invent a fifth category.
2. The body must be ONE line. A wrapped paragraph fails with 'body should contain exactly one line'. No trailing second sentence on its own line.
3. `authors:` must be a real GitHub login. `github-actions`, `claude`, and anything ending `[bot]` are rejected. Use the repo owner, Shivam-Fl — the same value .sdlc/agents/implementer.md mandates and 12 existing notes use.

Then run the repository's own check from the repo root and paste the passing line into the PR description:

    yarn workspaces focus @actual-app/ci-actions
    BASE_REF=main node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs

It must print `Validated 1 release note(s).` and exit 0. The note must be committed on the branch for the check to see it — the script diffs origin/main...HEAD against the worktree, so an uncommitted file reads as 'No release note added or modified'.

Do not touch any other file. There is no test to add: the note is data, and packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs already covers the checker's own rules.

alternatives_considered.approach: Run `yarn generate:release-notes` and answer the prompts.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: bin/release-note-generator.mts is an interactive `prompts` session — it shells out to `gh api user`, asks four questions on stdin and offers a select list. A non-interactive implementer cannot answer it, and the issue explicitly allows writing the file by hand when that is the path. The output the script would produce is the same three front-matter lines plus the one-line body, so hand-writing loses nothing.

alternatives_considered.approach: Use `category: Bugfixes` (the value in categoryOrder, and what two sibling notes in the directory already use).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: IAC-2 names `category: Bugfix` and so does the issue body; the checker accepts it via categoryAutocorrections, and it is the spelling the contributing docs list. Writing Bugfixes would satisfy the gate identically but contradict the criterion the ticket set, and QA reads the criterion.

It is on the NON_PERSON_AUTHORS denylist and the check fails it by name — verified by running the checker against such a note. It would also publish as '@github-actions' in the changelog, thanking a tool.

alternatives_considered.approach: Name the file with the PR number, e.g. `upcoming-release-notes/9.md`.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: IAC-1 requires a short descriptive slug rather than a number, and 70 of the 92 existing notes use descriptive slugs. Numeric names remain valid upstream but would fail this ticket's AC-1.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a vitest case to packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs asserting this note's front matter.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That suite already covers the checker's rules against synthetic notes; adding a case asserting one specific data file's contents tests the note, not the code, and would fail the moment anyone rewords the note. The change adds data, not behaviour.

assumptions: The repo owner Shivam-Fl is the correct human credit. They opened every other SDLC-authored note in this directory (12 of them), and .sdlc/agents/implementer.md:170 mandates $GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER over the bot or the model.

`category: Bugfix` is the intended spelling. The issue and IAC-2 both name it; the checker autocorrects it to `Bugfixes` before validating; packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md lists `Bugfix` as a valid category. Two other notes in the directory already use the bare `Bugfix` form, so it is the established local convention, not a typo.
unknowns: Whether the maintainer would prefer the body to mention 'Show empty rows' with the exact UI capitalization. I used the label as it appears in the report's own Options panel, which is the phrasing a user recognises.
risks: The one-line body rule is the likeliest silent failure: a naturally-worded note that wraps to two lines fails with 'body should contain exactly one line'. Write the single line as one physical line in the file; do not let an editor or formatter reflow it. `upcoming-release-notes/**` is not in .oxfmtrc.json's formatting scope as far as this work order can tell — if `yarn lint:fix` reflows the file, re-check it after linting.

Author rejection: `github-actions` (the PR author) and `claude` are on the NON_PERSON_AUTHORS denylist, and any login ending in `[bot]` is rejected. The only correct value here is the repo owner, Shivam-Fl. Getting this wrong fails the gate, and the error names the offending login, so it is recoverable.
The check reads origin/main...HEAD, so it reports 'No release note added or modified' if the note is not committed on the branch. Run it after committing, not before.

No risk path is touched. upcoming-release-notes/** is absent from forbidden_paths in .sdlc/config.yml, and no file under .github/**, .sdlc/**, .sdlc/memory/**, docs/spec/**, Dockerfile or AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md is created or edited.
